articles.title: 'This is unusual!' Jaws hit floor in CNN newsroom as Trump announces media ban
articles.description: President Donald Trump announced on Friday that the White House would be banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — and it left CNN's media analyst Brian Stelter scrambling to assess the situation. "Well this is unusual, isn't it?" Stelter told anchor Brianna Keilar. Stelter added that he is curious "what did CNN and MS NOW and Politico write that might have made the president so upset? And there is no specific answer in his post. There is no indication in that post." However, "there is no indication that the administration is taking any steps to actually follow through on his threat. So even though the threat is quite serious and would have real implications for the First Amendment and for the press freedom in the United States right now ... the CNN staff remains there, working like a normal Friday afternoon." Keilar noted that Trump has taken a number of potshots at CNN before, both publicly attacking them and trying to restrict their access to the government — to which Stelter concurred. In the most notable case, he said, "right after the midterms in 2018, during Trump's first term in office, he was angry about a question from our former CNN colleague, Jim Acosta, who was working here at the network for many years." After Acosta infuriated him at a press conference, Trump "took steps to revoke Acosta's press pass, and some viewers might remember that actually provoked a legal battle where CNN reluctantly ... [had] to go to court to defend that White House correspondent's First Amendment rights." Swiftly, a judge appointed by Trump himself ordered Acosta's press access reinstated , and he was back at work. And since then, Trump had largely not attempted to ban reporters or outlets altogether, noted Stelter. "There was an attempt to ban the Associated Press from some White House events," he said, in retaliation for not accepting Trump's guidelines renaming the Gulf of Mexico, "but we have not seen the president actually announce that he's banned news outlets altogether. And in this situation, we're in a little bit of a vacuum because, as I said, there's no indication that he's actually followed through. So let's give it a couple hours, see what happens." - YouTube www.youtube.com

articles.title: Trump Admin Covering Up Number of U.S. Troops Killed in Iran War
articles.description: The Trump administration may be hiding exactly how many American troops have died in the Iran war. The Washington Post , citing six anonymous U.S. officials, reports that more U.S. service members have died than the Department of Defense has publicly disclosed. Five of these officials told the newspaper that there have been 22 military deaths during the war, four more than the 18 currently appearing in the Defense Casualty Analysis System, the DoD’s public database. Another unnamed official says that 23 service members have been killed since February 28, when the U.S. and Israel first launched airstrikes on Iran. Not all of the alleged undisclosed deaths are directly tied to the war, this official reportedly said, but all of the deceased soldiers were in the Middle East while the war was going on. This official also told the Post that three American contractors based in the region have also died since the start of the war. The details behind the undisclosed deaths are unclear, including who they were and how, when, and where they died. The Pentagon refused to answer the newspaper’s inquiries about the disputed death figures. The Iran war is extremely unpopular with the American people, with the risk to U.S. troops among one of many reasons why. If Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and the rest of the Trump administration are hiding military casualties, that raises the question as to the circumstances of their deaths, and what incentive White House officials have to keep them secret. President Trump, Hegseth, and everyone else in the administration continue to insist that the Iran war is going well, despite the Strait of Hormuz remaining closed and Iran’s allies in Yemen, the Houthis, taking over the Bab al-Mandeb Strait on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula. Hiding American deaths further exposes the White House’s attempts to fool the American people that the war has been a success.
